headline: Bhatara gas leak: All 3 family members dead after explosion
summary: Fahima Akter, 21, died Saturday night, marking the third fatality in a tragic gas leak explosion at a building in Dhaka's Bhatara.
details: Fahima Akter, 21, passed away at the Sheikh Hasina National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery on Saturday night, according to residential physician Dr Shaon Bin Rahman.
She was the last surviving victim of a gas leak explosion that occurred on Tuesday at a six-storey building on 100-feet Road in Bhatara's Natun Bazar.
Her husband, Shahin, 24, died Friday morning with 50 percent burns, while Shahin's 8-year-old niece, Hafsa Akter, died early Thursday.
The explosion happened around 4:00 am on Tuesday. Neighbours reported hearing a loud blast at dawn and found the three victims severely burnt in their flat.
The flat was connected to a Titas Gas line, and a leakage was suspected to be the cause of the accident.
Fahima's aunt, Shamima Sultana, alleged that the landlord had been negligent. She claimed the family had noticed a gas smell shortly after moving in a month ago.
According to the aunt, although the landlord repaired the pipe once, repeated leaks were left unattended, leading to the tragedy.
caption:
A tragic gas leak explosion in Bhatara has claimed the lives of all three family members who lived in the flat.

Fahima Akter, 21, passed away at the Sheikh Hasina National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery on Saturday night, according to residential physician Dr Shaon Bin Rahman.

She was the last surviving victim of a gas leak explosion that occurred on Tuesday at a six-storey building on 100-feet Road in Bhatara's Natun Bazar.

Her husband, Shahin, 24, died Friday morning with 50 percent burns, while Shahin's 8-year-old niece, Hafsa Akter, died early Thursday.

The explosion happened around 4:00 am on Tuesday. Neighbours reported hearing a loud blast at dawn and found the three victims severely burnt in their flat.

The flat was connected to a Titas Gas line, and a leakage was suspected to be the cause of the accident.

Fahima's aunt, Shamima Sultana, alleged that the landlord had been negligent. She claimed the family had noticed a gas smell shortly after moving in a month ago.

According to the aunt, although the landlord repaired the pipe once, repeated leaks were left unattended, leading to the tragedy.

headline: Fastest bowler Nahid Rana ruled out of Australia series due to injury
summary: The 23-year-old pacer, known for his extreme speed, will be sidelined for 6-8 weeks after suffering a rib injury.
details: Bangladesh's fastest bowler, Nahid Rana, has been ruled out of the upcoming Test series against Australia. The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirmed that a rib injury on the left side will keep him out of action for six to eight weeks.

Rana's absence is a significant blow to the team as he has been one of the most consistent high-speed bowlers in Test cricket over the last two years. He currently holds the highest average speed of 141.54 km/h across 11 Tests, surpassing even Australia's Mitchell Starc.

The series was highly anticipated as a clash of speed between Rana and Starc. While Starc holds the record for the fastest single delivery (157.39 km/h), Rana's consistent high-speed deliveries make him a key asset for Bangladesh.

The team's pace attack is further weakened as left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam is also struggling with a hamstring injury. Shoriful is unlikely to feature in the first Test but may be considered for the second Test pending medical clearance.

Bangladesh will play their first Test against Australia on August 13 in Darwin and the second on August 22 in Mackay. This marks the team's first Test tour of Australia since 2003, nearly two decades later.
